newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tajiks deny Afghan factions using their air bases.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks deny Afghan factions using their air bases.

text.p: Tajikistan's government said on Tuesday no warplanes belonging to any faction from neighbouring Afghanistan were using bases on its territory.
On Monday, Afghanistan's radical Islamic Taleban militia accused Tajikistan of allowing anti-Taleban forces to use air bases in the former Soviet republic, itself devastated by a four-year civil war.

"This does not correspond to reality," Zafar Saidov, spokesman for Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, told Reuters by telephone from the Tajik capital Dushanbe. "There were no and are no Afghan warplanes (on Tajik territory)," he said.
He described the Taleban accusation as a "provocation".

However, some observers in Tajikistan say anti-Taleban commander Ahmad Shah Masood has for several months used an air base near the southern Tajik town of Kulyab to transport materiel by helicopter to his bases in northern Afghanistan.
The Taleban, which control over three quarters of Afghanistan, are seeking to bring the remaining six northeastern and central provinces under their control.
The former Soviet republics of Central Asia, including Tajikistan, fear a possible Taleban advance in the spring towards their borders could destabilise their own fragile nations.
